narrative: The model estimated a 56% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt—slightly more likely than not to fail—so your law school application was denied. The strongest factor was your undergraduate GPA of 2.80, which is below the 3.23 average among accepted students; this lower academic record pushed the prediction toward failure. The second most influential factor was your LSAT score of 37.00, essentially in line with the accepted-student average of 37.18; this factor slightly pushed toward passing and was the main counterweight in your file. The third factor was your third-year class decile of 5.00, below the accepted average of 5.79, which also pushed toward failure by suggesting weaker recent academic standing. Although your first-year decile was strong, it was not among the three largest influences. To improve your chances if you reapply, focus on demonstrating stronger academic performance, such as additional coursework or a post-baccalaureate program; consult an admissions adviser about how to address the GPA and third-year standing; and prepare a clear plan showing readiness for law study and bar passage.
